jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Site Reliability Engineering
jobs.description:
As a TPM for SRE, you will partner with SRE leaders and engineers to scale the platform that underpins all of MongoDB’s cloud products. You will drive program execution, strengthen production reliability practices, and coordinate cross-functional efforts across US and EMEA teams. Success in this role means smoother launches, clearer roadmaps, stronger reliability metrics and an SRE organization that's better-equipped to deliver predictability at scale.

This role can be based out of our Dublin or Cork office or remotely in Ireland.

What You'll Do

Drive Program Planning & Execution – Define program scope, milestones, and success criteria with SRE engineers and leaders. Manage dependencies across platform teams, keep work clearly tracked in Jira, and deliver on time
Strengthen Production Reliability – Lead change management and launch readiness programs. Partner with SREs and product teams to define and operationalize SLOs/SLIs, and use incident data, metrics, and capacity signals to drive prioritization and continuous improvement
Lead Cross-Functional Coordination – Align SRE with Security, Compliance, Cloud platform, and other engineering teams. Coordinate cross-team incident response, ensure clear follow-through, and build trust as the go-to driver of complex, multi-team efforts
Build Scalable Systems & Processes – Design lightweight frameworks and communication patterns that help SRE deliver reliably at scale. Work yourself out of the "hero" role by leaving teams better-equipped to execute independently

Requirements

8+ years in technical program management, engineering management, or a comparable technical role partnering with software engineering teams
Proven track record leading large-scale, cross-team platform initiatives through ambiguity and change
Strong knowledge of production change management, software development lifecycle, and reliability metrics (SLOs, SLIs)
Skilled at shaping roadmaps and managing dependencies
Able to query and interpret metrics, logs, or other data sources to inform decisions and communicate risk
Excellent communicator—clear, concise, and calm—across engineers, cross-functional partners, and executives
Low-ego, highly collaborative, and motivated by ownership of hard problems end to end

Nice to Have

Hands-on or close-partner experience with Kubernetes, cloud networking, or observability stacks (metrics, logs, tracing, alerting)
Prior experience working with or alongside SRE teams
Background in large-scale cloud infrastructure or platform engineering
Familiarity with MongoDB Atlas or other modern cloud database platforms

Why This Role

This role puts MongoDB's values into practice. You'll own hard, ambiguous problems end to end. You'll build together with SRE, engineering, Security, and Compliance to co-create solutions that work across the organization. And you'll think big—scaling the platform and practices that power MongoDB's next phase of growth. You'll be in the critical path of high-impact projects, working with executive stakeholders, and supported to grow in your career.

About MongoDB

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including 75% of the Fortune 100 and AI-native startups, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It’s what makes us MongoDB.

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we’re committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees’ wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it’s like to work at MongoDB, and help us make an impact on the world!

MongoDB is an equal opportunities employer.

jobs.title: Principal IT Security Project Manager
jobs.description:
Bullhorn's core purpose is to create an incredible customer experience, and the organization has a sharp focus on delivering very high quality products and services to its customers. The company culture is shaped by five Core Values: Ownership, Energy, Speed & Agility, Service, and Being Human. Each value, and its underlying definition, serves as a behavioral guide for employees as they interact with customers and fellow coworkers and is an embedded way of operating across our organization.

Bullhorn is a fast-paced and dynamic environment where hard work and outstanding results are rewarded and celebrated. We value those that exhibit an eagerness to learn and a strong natural desire for continuous improvement and we encourage team members to stretch themselves, acknowledge challenges and learn from them. With a strong focus on growth, we provide ample opportunities for career development and prioritize promoting from within. We believe that leaders should care deeply about the development of their employees at all levels, emphasizing emotional intelligence and accountability. Our leaders collaborate closely to ensure the success of their teams, and we work together to achieve shared goals, creating a challenging and rewarding workplace for everyone.

About The Role

A Principal IT Security Project Manager
leads complex, enterprise-wide cybersecurity initiatives and manages strategic security programs from planning to completion. As a SaaS provider, Bullhorn’s security posture is critical to our customers' continued success. This role will be part of the Information Security vertical, reporting directly to the CISO.

A Typical Day Will Include...

Program Leadership: Direct large-scale cross-functional security projects, such as large scale software hardening, identity management rollouts, cloud security implementations, or zero-trust implementations.
Risk Management: Identify project risks, track vulnerabilities, and build mitigation plans to protect business assets.
Stakeholder Management: Communicate project progress, budgets, and security metrics clearly to executive leadership and technical teams. Ability to present progress in both concise headlines and detailed technical detail.
Resource Allocation: Manage solution planning calls, team workloads, and identifying budget issues/needs.
Compliance Alignment: Ensure all project milestones meet regulatory standards where applicable (SOC 2, ISO 27001)

This Role Is a Fit for You If...

Experience: You have 8+ years of IT project management experience, with at least 5 years focused specifically on cybersecurity or information security.
Education: You have a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Business, or a related field.
Certifications: You have a PMP (Project Management Professional) and a security credential like CISSP, CISM, or CRISC.
Technical Knowledge: You have a deep understanding of network security, endpoint protection, threat intelligence, and security frameworks.
Leadership: You have a proven ability to lead cross-functional teams without direct authority.
Communication: You have exceptional verbal and written communication skills for translating technical security risks into business language.
Work Style: You are comfortable being self motivated and working independently. Ability to work seamlessly with executives and engineers as needed.

The annual base salary range for this position is $144,000 - $170,000. In addition, this role is eligible for an annual target bonus & a comprehensive benefits package.

Compensation And Transparency Statement

The posted range represents the good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. Actual pay within the range will be based on factors such as, but not limited to, experience, skills, qualifications, geographic location, internal equity, and business or organizational needs and affordability. In accordance with state and local pay transparency laws we disclose salary ranges in all job postings and provide additional information upon request.

What We Offer...

Benefits eligibility effective DAY ONE including Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), 401(k) Match, and more
Unlimited Planned Paid Time Off
Global Mental Health Support
On-Demand Learning & Development
Quarterly paid volunteer days
Lucrative Employee Referral Program (eligible for prior to your first day)
Company-wide mentor program

Are you passionate about human space exploration, understanding the origins of the universe, and working with a passionate and diverse team to make a difference? If you are, we need you!

We need you to bring creative ideas and diverse backgrounds to help us envision, shape, and deliver systems that will enable the exploration of space while benefiting people here on Earth. As NASA’s largest engineering solutions provider working together with NASA at centers across the United States.

Oversee the day-to-day operations of Citadel's Customer Lease Finance partners and processes, keeping agreements, approvals, and funding statuses accurate and on time.
Manage, coach, and develop a team of lease coordinators, including workload planning, performance goals, and training, and hold the team to target timelines and SLAs.

Identify risks, dependencies, and resource conflicts early, and drive resolution with stakeholders and leadership.

Required

Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to lead meetings, including with executives and external partners.
2+ years of experience managing a team, ideally in an operations environment.

jobs.title: Grant Program Manager, Future Ready Graduates
jobs.description:
Job Profile

Administrative Operations Specialist 3

Job Family

Administrative Operations

Time Type

Full time

Apply before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted End Date.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree and five (5) years of experience appropriate to the area of assignment/field; OR, Any equivalent combination of experience and/or training from which comparable knowledge, skills and abilities have been achieved.

Job Profile Summary

Supports and instructs those served by the department with complex queries, applies specialized knowledge of multiple standards, policies and procedures, and maintains accurate and detailed records.

Job Description

Salary Range:
$75,000 - $85,000 per year; DOE

About The University Innovation Alliance

The University Innovation Alliance is a national coalition of public research universities working together to improve student success and post graduate economic mobility, particularly for low-income students, first-generation college students, and students of color. UIA member institutions collaborate to design, test, refine, and scale practices that help more students persist, graduate, and successfully transition from college to careers. In 2025, the UIA aligned on expanded impact goals. One of the expanded goals is focused on improving value and mobility for students. The future ready graduates initiative is a direct result of the UIA now focusing on student success beyond degree completion. The UIA has secured 2 grant projects under this initiative and anticipates securing another 2 in the next year.

About Future Ready Graduates

Future Ready Graduates is UIA’s portfolio of work focused on helping member institutions expand and improve the number of work based learning experiences available to students to support their career preparation and employment outcomes. Current FRG projects are focused on work integrated learning redesign (focus on internships and project based learning) and student employment redesign leveraging a partnership with the Work + team at ASU. Through coordinated grant-funded initiatives, UIA supports campuses in redesigning student experiences, improving access to meaningful paid opportunities, strengthening employer partnerships, and connecting work-based learning more directly to persistence, completion, and career outcomes.

Position Summary

The Grant Program Manager, Future Ready Graduates is responsible for the day-to-day delivery, implementation, coordination, and program management of UIA’s Future Ready Graduates grant portfolio. The position will initially manage delivery of two active awards and may assume responsibility for up to two additional awards.

The Program Manager will coordinate participating campuses, partners, consultants, employers, and internal UIA contributors to ensure that project activities are completed on time, meet funder commitments, and achieve the expected level of quality. This role will maintain project plans, monitor campus progress, facilitate meetings and events, organize employer feedback processes, maintain accurate records in Salesforce and Google Drive, and represent program implementation during funder meetings and written updates.

The ideal candidate is a highly organized and collaborative program manager who can manage multiple grants and campus workstreams simultaneously. This person will be skilled at setting clear expectations, holding partners accountable, identifying risks early, and helping campus teams translate project requirements into practical implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Grant Portfolio Management

Manage the implementation and operations of two active Future Ready Graduates awards, with the potential to manage up to two additional related awards.
Translate grant agreements, workplans, budgets, milestones, and funder commitments into coordinated implementation plans.
Develop and maintain project plans that identify activities, owners, deadlines, dependencies, decision points, and required deliverables.
Monitor implementation across all assigned awards and provide regular updates on progress, risks, delays, and resource needs.
Ensure work is delivered on time, within the approved scope, and at the level of quality expected by UIA and its funding partners.
Coordinate overlapping activities and shared deliverables across awards so that the Future Ready Graduates portfolio operates as a cohesive body of work.
Support grant launch, implementation, reporting, evaluation, dissemination, and closeout activities.

Campus Implementation and Accountability

Serve as a primary point of contact for campus teams participating in assigned Future Ready Graduates projects.
Lead campus onboarding and establish clear expectations for participation, implementation, reporting, and deliverable quality.
Help campuses translate grant requirements into campus-specific implementation plans, milestones, and workstreams.
Monitor progress toward campus deliverables and follow up regularly to address missed deadlines, incomplete work, or implementation barriers.
Review campus submissions and project materials for completeness, alignment, and quality.
Coordinate coaching, technical assistance, and problem-solving support with ASU Work+, consultants, evaluators, and other subject-matter experts.
Maintain regular communication with campus leads and ensure institutional teams remain engaged throughout the project period.

Employer Engagement and Feedback Loops

Work with UIA colleagues and campus teams to recruit and engage employers as project advisors, co-design partners, and sources of ongoing feedback.
Establish and maintain structured employer feedback loops across the Future Ready Graduates portfolio.
Plan employer listening sessions, validation meetings, feedback activities, and other engagement opportunities.
Ensure employer perspectives inform program design, student journey redesign, implementation testing, and refinement.
Document employer feedback and help campus teams translate it into actionable program or system improvements.
Track how employer input influences campus decisions and project outcomes. Employer feedback is intended to be embedded throughout the redesign cycle, including discovery, prototype validation, implementation, and planning for scale.

Meetings, Convenings, and Project Events

Plan and coordinate project-based meetings, campus working sessions, communities of practice, workshops, employer sessions, and in-person convenings.
Develop agendas, participant materials, timelines, run-of-show documents, and follow-up communications.
Facilitate selected meetings and working sessions and coordinate facilitation by ASU Work+, consultants, or other partners.
Organize cross-campus learning opportunities that allow institutions to compare progress, troubleshoot barriers, and refine their approaches.
Coordinate event logistics in partnership with UIA’s Campus Engagement & Events Manager and operations staff.
Capture decisions, action items, and follow-up responsibilities after project meetings.

Funder Engagement and Reporting

Prepare updates, project summaries, briefing materials, and talking points for funder meetings.
Maintain documentation needed to demonstrate progress against funder commitments.
Identify risks or changes that may require early communication, funder guidance, or formal approval.
Support preparation of continuation requests, change requests, final reports, and grant-closeout materials.

Project Records and Knowledge Management

Maintain complete, accurate, and current project records in Salesforce and Google Drive.
Establish and maintain a clear folder structure, naming conventions, version-control practices, and documentation standards.
Record campus participation, meetings, milestones, deliverables, decisions, risks, employer engagement, and follow-up activities in Salesforce.
Ensure key documents, reports, workplans, participant materials, and final deliverables are stored consistently and accessible to the appropriate team members.
Maintain project calendars, trackers, contact lists, reporting schedules, and shared implementation tools.
Support development of standard templates and processes that can be used across the Future Ready Graduates portfolio.

Progress Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Capture

Track progress toward grant milestones, deliverables, campus participation targets, and intended outcomes.
Coordinate collection of implementation updates, participation data, feedback, and supporting documentation from campuses and partners.
Work with evaluators and internal partners to ensure campuses understand data requirements and submit information on schedule.
Identify common implementation barriers, promising practices, and conditions that influence success across participating institutions.
Help translate project learning into case studies, playbooks, implementation guides, employer-feedback resources, and other materials for broader diffusion.
Support final evaluation, synthesis, dissemination, and planning for scale.
Design and develop evaluation frameworks, data collection instruments, templates, surveys, interview protocols, rubrics, dashboards, and reporting processes that enable campuses to consistently collect, analyze, and use implementation and outcome data.
Design AI-enabled workflows that transform complex institutional data into actionable insights, scalable evaluation processes, and decision-making resources.

The Future Ready Graduates work plan calls for shared resources such as campus case studies, dashboard guidance, employer feedback-loop templates, implementation guidance, and a strategy for broader diffusion.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Work across UIA’s program, learning, development, finance, operations, communications, and campus-engagement functions.
Establish clear ownership, review processes, and deadlines for work requiring contributions from multiple teams.
Coordinate with the Business Operations & Finance Manager on budgets, campus stipends, contracts, and grant-related financial processes.
Coordinate with communications staff on external storytelling, case studies, dissemination, and project visibility.
Perform other duties as assigned in support of Future Ready Graduates and UIA’s student-success portfolio.

Desired Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in higher education, education, workforce development, nonprofit management, public administration, project management, or a related field.
3-5 years of relevant experience in program management, grant implementation, higher education, workforce development, student success, or a related area.
Demonstrated experience managing multiple complex projects or grants with overlapping milestones and stakeholder groups.
Strong experience managing workplans, deliverables, deadlines, risks, and cross-functional dependencies.
Ability to hold partners and participating teams accountable while maintaining constructive, collaborative relationships.
Experience organizing and facilitating meetings, convenings, workshops, or communities of practice.
Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and follow-through.
Ability to manage several active workstreams and adjust priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work independently while maintaining consistent communication across a distributed team.
Commitment to improving career readiness and postsecondary outcomes for students.
Experience using Salesforce, Google Workspace, and project-management platforms.
Experience working in a remote team environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with student employment, paid work-based learning, internships, career readiness, experiential learning, or employer engagement.
Experience managing a portfolio of related grants or initiatives.
Experience working with employer partners and developing structured feedback or advisory processes.
Familiarity with design thinking, human-centered design, service design, process map

As Technical Program Manager, you will drive AI-led ServiceNow builds from first idea through delivery and adoption. You will work alongside the pod Architect, AI / Now Assist Engineer, Leads, and Developers, turning ambiguous business goals into clear milestones and removing whatever slows the team down. You will be a first point of contact for client stakeholders on build progress, risks, and escalations.

What you'll do

Plan and structure the build

• Turn complex, ambiguous problems into prioritized milestones, deliverables, and success criteria, translating business objectives into a tactical and strategic execution plan.
• Build and manage integrated schedules across Now Assist, AI Agent, workflow, integration, and data workstreams.
• Define measurable outcomes with the Architect and track value delivered to LOB leaders.
Drive execution

• Run large, cross-functional, high-visibility AI builds on condensed timelines.
• Coordinate day-to-day activities across the pod and client teams; hold owners accountable for their commitments.
• Anticipate and remove obstacles, especially around AI deployment, data readiness, security review, and environment access.
Risk, release, and governance

• Manage risks, dependencies, and impediments; escalate early with a recommended path forward.
• Manage releases and navigate AI release requirements, including AI governance, responsible-AI review, security, and client change-management standards.
• Drive root cause analysis and post-incident reviews to closure; track corrective actions.
Client relationships and reporting

• Build trusted relationships with client technology leaders, LOB stakeholders, and sponsors.
• Act as first point of contact or escalation for build progress and delivery issues.
• Create transparency through status reports, dashboards, and executive updates.
Continuous improvement

• Improve delivery processes and document best practices; use automation to replace repetitive operational tasks.
• Turn one-off wins into reusable patterns and playbooks for future pods.
• Give and seek feedback to build an open, collaborative team culture.

Required qualifications

• 10+ years of project or program management experience in software delivery, consulting, or SaaS organizations.
• 3+ years managing ServiceNow programs or implementations.
• Solid understanding of SDLC and release management for cloud-based SaaS platforms.
• Delivered AI or intelligent-workflow solutions into production with measurable client impact.
• Familiarity with AI governance, compliance, and enterprise security practices.
• Strong program management practice: planning, schedule management, risk and dependency management, change management, and predictive metrics.

As a CPS Manager, you will design and implement effective project and programme management strategies for clients across multiple industries. You will work closely with senior leaders of major global organisations to improve the efficiency of their capital programmes, support the achievement of project objectives, and provide guidance to clients managing projects within tight budget constraints. You will also assist clients in overcoming project delivery challenges. The role will be predominately focussed on the UK market, which you will typically support remotely from the ETIC. Selecting and deploying new project management software, training staff, and embedding new ways of working to improve transparency and reporting.

• Communicates confidently and delivers clear, impactful messages to a range of audiences to influence outcomes.

• Demonstrates leadership skills and a strong commitment to coaching and developing others.

• Possesses strong technical and analytical abilities, with the capacity to simplify complex issues and deliver practical client solutions.

Job Description

Lead Client Growth Across the NY/NJ Water Market

This is not a traditional project management role. WSP is seeking a proven seller-doer to help expand our water and wastewater business throughout New Jersey and the New York metropolitan region. This role offers the opportunity to shape market strategy, grow key client relationships, and influence the future direction of a rapidly expanding practice.

As a Senior Project Manager / Client Service Leader, you will serve as a trusted advisor to municipal utilities, sewerage authorities, and public-sector clients — while building WSP's presence across one of the most active infrastructure markets in the country.

Why This Role Is Different

The NJ/NY market is defined by complexity — NJDEP and NYSDEC permitting environments, a dense network of municipal utilities and sewerage authorities operating under consent decrees and capital improvement mandates, and significant federal investment flowing through EPA and BIL grant programs. Navigating this environment takes relationships, regulatory fluency, and the ability to position a firm for programs before they go to bid. WSP is investing in this market and this role is the platform to lead that effort.

Significant opportunity to grow existing accounts and develop new clients across the region
Ability to shape regional strategy and investment priorities
Access to national technical resources while maintaining local market leadership
Pathway toward Client Director, Growth Leader, and Regional Leadership positions

What You'll Do

Develop and expand relationships with NJ and NY municipalities, municipal utilities, sewerage authorities, and MUAs
Lead strategic pursuits, positioning, proposals, interviews, and contract negotiations
Serve as trusted advisor to key clients on major capital programs
Manage major infrastructure programs and multidisciplinary teams through planning, design, and construction
Mentor project managers and technical staff
Support regional growth initiatives and market planning

PE license in NJ or NY required, or ability to obtain through reciprocity
12+ years of municipal water/wastewater consulting experience
Established relationships with NJ and/or NY municipal utilities, authorities, and agencies
Demonstrated business development success in the NJ/NY market

jobs.title: Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Description – Business Analyst

Role overview

We are hiring a Business Analyst to own how our systems, data and processes work together — from gathering requirements to building, automating, reporting and training, with AI used as a core part of how the work gets done.

On any given day you may map a process, write a spec, build an automation, fix a CRM layout, produce a dashboard, run a project stand-up or train a team. You will act as the bridge between the business and the tech stack, and turn messy problems into clear, working solutions.

Key responsibilities

AI-led delivery (day to day)

Use AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Zia) daily to speed up requirements, documentation, analysis, testing and build work.

Design and deploy AI-powered workflows: agents, assistants, classification, summarisation, data enrichment and AI-generated content inside business systems.

Write, test and maintain prompts and prompt templates; evaluate AI output for accuracy, tone and risk before it reaches staff or customers.

Connect AI models to business systems through APIs, MCP servers and automation platforms.

Proactively identify where AI can replace manual tasks, and measure time saved.

Keep up with new AI tools and features, run quick pilots and recommend what to adopt.

Apply responsible AI practice: data privacy, access control, human review and clear usage guidelines.

Business analysis (functional and technical)

Run stakeholder workshops and interviews to capture requirements, pain points and success criteria.

Map current-state and future-state processes; identify gaps, waste, automation and AI opportunities.

Write clear BRDs, functional specs, user stories, acceptance criteria and technical specs (data models, field mappings, API and integration logic).

Translate business needs into system configuration and build‑ready designs, and validate delivered work against requirements.

Data analysis and business intelligence

Clean, audit and maintain data quality across CRM and operational systems (duplicates, picklists, field hygiene, ownership).

Build and maintain dashboards, KPIs and recurring reports for leadership and operational teams.

Use AI-assisted analysis to surface trends, insights and recommended actions.

Write queries and data transformations to support reporting and decision-making.

Project management

Plan and deliver system and process projects end to end: scope, timeline, risks, dependencies and sign-off.

Run sprints, stand-ups and status updates; keep tasks, priorities and blockers visible.

Manage multiple concurrent workstreams and re-prioritise quickly as business needs change.

Automation and integration

Design and build workflow automations, blueprints and custom functions (e.g. Zoho Deluge, Make.com scenarios, GoHighLevel workflows).

Build and maintain integrations between platforms using APIs, webhooks and connectors.

Identify and implement AI and automation opportunities that remove manual work.

Monitor automations for failures and fix them quickly.

Tech stack management and system administration

Administer core platforms: users, roles, profiles, permissions, modules, layouts, fields and templates.

Maintain the tech stack inventory, licences, access and vendor relationships; recommend tools to add, consolidate or retire.

Own change management: test in sandbox, document changes and release safely.

Handle tier‑2 system support and troubleshooting for internal users.

Training, documentation and best practice

Create SOPs, user guides, process maps and training materials for every system or process change, using AI to produce and maintain them faster.

Deliver onboarding and refresher training to staff, live and recorded.

Define and enforce system, data and AI standards, naming conventions and governance; train staff to use AI tools effectively and safely.

Team management

Lead, guide and review the work of junior analysts, admins or offshore support staff.

Allocate tasks, set priorities and quality‑check output.

Coach team members and contribute to hiring and onboarding new team members.

Requirements

Must have

3–5 years in a business analyst, systems analyst or business systems role, covering both functional and technical BA work.

Demonstrated daily use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or similar) to accelerate analysis, documentation and build work, with examples to show.

Hands‑on experience building AI-powered automations: calling LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and embedding AI steps into workflows (e.g. via Make.com, Zoho Flow or n8n).

Sound judgement on AI output quality, data privacy and when human review is needed.

Hands‑on administration of at least one major CRM (Zoho CRM strongly preferred; Salesforce or HubSpot considered).

Proven experience building workflow automations and integrations (APIs, webhooks, JSON, low-code tools such as Make.com, Zapier or Zoho Flow).

Strong data skills: Excel / Google Sheets (advanced), SQL or similar query language, and a BI tool (Zoho Analytics, Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau).

Experience managing projects with defined scope, timelines and stakeholders, using tools such as Zoho Projects, Jira or Asana.

Experience writing requirements, user stories, process maps (BPMN or swimlane) and SOPs.

Experience delivering user training and supporting adoption of new systems.

Excellent written and spoken English.

Nice to have

Scripting experience (Zoho Deluge, JavaScript or Python).

Advanced AI experience: building AI agents, MCP servers, RAG / knowledge-base assistants or multi-step AI workflows.

Experience across the wider Zoho One suite (Desk, Recruit, Creator, Sprints, Learn, Cliq).

Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 administration.

Prior experience leading or mentoring a small team.

Experience supporting Australian businesses or working with remote teams across time zones.

Relevant certification (e.g. Zoho CRM Certified Administrator, IIBA ECBA/CCBA, PMP/CAPM, Agile/Scrum, or an AI/LLM course).

What we’re looking for

AI-first mindset.

Your default question is "how can AI make this faster or better?", and you back it with working solutions.

Strong communicator.

You explain technical ideas in plain language, write clearly, ask the right questions and keep stakeholders informed without being chased.

Highly organised.

You juggle many requests, prioritise by impact and urgency, and keep your work documented and traceable.

Fast turnaround.

You move quickly, deliver in iterations and don't let small tasks sit.

Multi-dimensional problem solver.

You consider the process, the people, the data and the system together, not just the immediate symptom.

Solution- and process-driven.

You bring a recommended fix, not just a problem, and you design repeatable processes rather than one‑off workarounds.

Ownership mindset.

You take responsibility end to end, from requirement to adoption, and work well with limited supervision.

Aggregate data and produce reports to represent status and results
Conduct strategic, tactical and quantitative analysis in support of security investigations and operations

jobs.title: Protective Intelligence Analyst- OSINT Monitoring and Triage
jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly capable Protective Intelligence Analyst to support the protection of senior Vanguard executives globally. This role requires an experienced OSINT practitioner who can independently manage threat identification and triage, prioritize competing executive protection needs, and produce decision-ready intelligence products under time pressure. The position owns the threat identification and initial assessment function for Vanguard’s protective intelligence program, including the daily monitoring and alert queue through which every inbound threat communication, platform alert, and referral receives its initial assessment. The Protective Intelligence Analyst will distinguish credible concerns from noise, open cases for identified security concerns, and manage case tracking and related metrics for the program. The role offers broad exposure across the protective intelligence lifecycle and meaningful ownership of threat intake, applying structured analytic judgment to determine which matters warrant escalation or further investigation.

Monitoring & Triage

Manage daily alert and intake queues: vendor alerting feeds, the program’s intake channels, executive-assistant and partner referrals, and regional intelligence routing.
Triage inbound items against the program’s established threat screening criteria; disposition items as unfounded with documented rationale or open cases for investigation.
Provide dedicated monitoring coverage during executive travel and event windows, assessing emerging developments in real time and escalating per defined criteria.
Maintain watchlist hygiene and help fine tune OSINT feeds to ensure reliable threat identification.

Case Management & Intelligence Production

Maintain key protective intelligence trackers/metrics: request log, alert log, case entries, product IDs, and dashboard integrity.
Conduct OSINT collection and analysis for protective intelligence assessments, documenting sources and findings and contributing analytic judgments to final products.
Draft the program’s weekly intelligence summary, synthesizing alert activity, case developments, and emerging threat trends into concise, decision-ready reporting.
Process intake acknowledgements and maintain records-handling standards for intake channels.

Team Model – Primary Focus, Universal Capability

Triage and monitoring is the primary focus of this role, not an exclusive lane. Every Protective Intelligence Analyst trains to produce the program’s core assessment products to standard, rotates through triage and monitoring coverage, and serves as designated backup for at least one other product line, so the team carries no single points of failure.
Cross-train teammates in triage and monitoring, maintain current proficiency in teammates’ specialties, and participate in the program’s dual-review and after-action practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security studies, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Minimum of three years of related experience in a field such as intelligence analysis, GSOC/watch operations, journalism/research, or military/law-enforcement analysis.
Demonstrated ability to work a high-volume queue with consistency, accuracy, and documented decisions.
Strong OSINT skills, including the ability to locate, verify, and assess the credibility of information across open sources.
Comfort with reading concerning or threatening content professionally and escalating appropriately.
High ethical standards and discretion when handling sensitive executive and corporate information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders clearly and calmly under time pressure.
Proven ability to think critically and assess incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with threat intelligence, alerting, or case management platforms.
Formal training or applied experience in threat assessment, targeted violence prevention, or intelligence analysis.
ATAP membership, with active interest or progress toward obtaining the Certified Threat Manager (CTM) designation.

Special Factors

Participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours escalation support as the program matures.
Early-morning queue coverage; occasional evening and weekend surge coverage during executive travel windows.

jobs.location: Tel Aviv-Yafo, Tel Aviv District, Israel
jobs.description:
Money is becoming software. That changes everything about how it has to be protected. Stablecoins, tokenized assets, and payments made by AI agents are moving real value at machine speed. That’s where Blockaid comes in. We build the security technology behind how money moves. Coinbase, MetaMask, Uniswap, and many of the largest platforms moving money today rely on us to screen billions of transactions and stop fraud, scams, and hacks before they reach a single user.

We’re backed by investors including Sequoia Capital, Ribbit Capital, and Cyberstarts, firms behind some of the biggest names in cybersecurity.

We’re looking for a Threat Intelligence Analyst to join our threat intelligence team and track the cybercriminals targeting crypto. You’ll dig into attackers’ TTPs across on-chain and off-chain sources, from the dark web to messaging apps, turning OSINT and HUMINT into intelligence reports and prevention strategies that protect millions of users.

What You'll Do:

Track and evaluate crypto-focused cybercriminals, including the tools, techniques, and procedures used by attackers, their motivations, and industry-wide trends.

Produce and present intelligence reports on relevant threat groups and campaigns, detailing methodologies and the motivations driving the activities.

Research both on-chain and off-chain crypto attack vectors, identifying attacker interests and uncovering root causes behind incidents.

Help develop prevention strategies and detection mechanisms to mitigate future attacks.

Collect and manage information from diverse sources such as social media platforms, messaging apps, forums, the dark web, news feeds, and other open and covert channels.

Use advanced tools and investigative techniques, including OSINT and HUMINT methodologies, to generate accurate and relevant intelligence.

Communicate with customers about potential risks and threats, and work closely with Customer Success, Marketing, and Sales.

Requirements:

3+ years of experience in intelligence analysis, with a focus on WEBINT / OSINT.

Strong understanding of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), the cybercrime ecosystem, and underground information sources.

Excellent analytical thinking and report-writing skills

Fluent English, written and spoken.

Familiarity with AI coding and automation tools and ability to build automated processes, analyze data and build visualizations for threat reporting

Nice to have:

Experience with blockchain technologies and a solid grasp of the Web3 ecosystem and its threats.

Analyze merchant chargeback performance (recovery rate, win rate, volumes, trends) and explain what's driving changes.
Break down performance by PSP, card scheme, reason code and dispute type to find gaps and improvement opportunities.
Identify and drive optimizations, such as data enrichment gaps, evidence and argument improvements, and fight/don't-fight strategy. Measure their impact.
Prepare data-driven QBRs/EBRs and client-facing performance reports with the CSM and SE teams.
Build and maintain dashboards and recurring reports that track client health and key commercial metrics.
Run root-cause analysis when performance drops and recommend clear next steps.
Spot upsell and expansion opportunities from client data, such as pre-dispute alerts and new coverage.

Turn recurring client needs into structured feedback and requirements for Product.
Present findings and recommendations clearly to internal stakeholders and clients.

Degree in Industrial Engineering, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or another quantitative field. A master's degree is an advantage.
3–5+ years of experience as a business, data or commercial analyst, ideally in a client-facing or B2B environment.
Advanced SQL.
Proficiency with BI/analytics tools (e.g., Tableau).

Strong business sense, with the ability to connect data to commercial outcomes and client value.
Excellent communication skills, comfortable presenting insights to clients and senior stakeholders.
Experience in a customer-facing analytics role (e.g., supporting CS/AM, preparing business reviews) is an advantage.
Understanding of chargebacks, payments, PSPs or fraud prevention in fintech or e-commerce is an advantage.

jobs.title: Program Manager - Housing Stability
jobs.description:
Agate is seeking two Housing Stability Program Managers to provides leadership, supervision, and program oversight for Agate's resident services at assigned Minneapolis Public Housing Authority (MPHA) Asset Management Projects (AMPs) and properties in the South or North Team service area. The position supports a consistent, housing-focused approach to resident engagement, case management, eviction prevention, resource coordination, and housing stability across properties serving varied resident populations. The Program Manager supervises assigned Case Managers and other designated Team staff, partners closely with MPHA regional and onsite property management teams, and ensures that resident services align with contract requirements, agency practices, and the needs of each community. The role includes scheduled resident-facing presence, staff coaching and case consultation, and coordination with Agate's specialized crisis, targeted intervention, and benefits staff when residents need additional support. This is an in-office position, with flexibility for occasional remote work or adjustments to daily schedule as operational needs allow. Core working hours fall between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., with flexibility in start and end times. Compensation: $70,000__________________________________________________________________________________ Why Work at Agate Housing and Services?
At Agate Housing and Services, we believe everyone deserves a safe place to call home, and we are passionate about making that a reality. What makes Agate special is not just the work we do, but the people who do it. Our team is made up of compassionate, dedicated, and driven individuals who show up every day with a shared commitment to making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. We foster a workplace where people support one another, bring new ideas forward, embrace challenges, and take pride in the impact of their work. When you join Agate, you become part of a team that is bigger than any one person, united by a mission to end homelessness and relieve hunger through action and advocacy. If you are looking for meaningful work, great people, and the opportunity to make a lasting difference in your community, we would love to have you be part of Agate! Benefit OverviewPaid Holidays: Agate provides paid holidays, including New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day, plus additional floating holidays. Full-time employees receive up to 88 hours of holiday pay annually, prorated for part-time employees and employees who start during the year. Most agency operations are closed on fixed holidays.See Agate's career page for more information about our benefit plans. Agate offers health insurance through Medica, with traditional and high-deductible plans available across three popular networks, including M Health Fairview and HealthPartners, among others. Agate pays 100% of dental and life insurance premiums and contributes 1.5% of each employee's salary to their retirement account, even if the employee does not contribute. Position Responsibilities:

Provide day-to-day supervision, leadership, coaching, and performance support to assigned MPHA Team staff; set clear expectations for resident engagement, housing stabilization, responsiveness, and documentation.
Conduct regular individual supervision, team meetings, case consultation, and professional development activities that promote consistent, high-quality services and staff accountability.
Oversee service delivery across assigned AMPs and properties, adjusting staff priorities and resident engagement approaches to the needs of senior and disability housing, family housing, mixed-population communities, and other assigned properties.
Maintain active, collaborative relationships with MPHA regional and onsite property management teams; establish clear communication, referral, escalation, and follow-up practices.
Support staff in early identification of housing stability concerns, including lease compliance, rent or income changes, resident conflict, and barriers to accessing services; coordinate prevention-oriented responses and follow-through.
Maintain scheduled resident-facing hours at assigned properties through outreach, resident meetings, service coordination, or direct support appropriate to the managerial role.
Provide case consultation and assist staff with complex resident needs, conflicts, and situations requiring coordinated involvement of property management, specialized Agate staff, or community providers.
Coordinate with the LICSW Provider and Crisis & Float Team on urgent resident concerns, targeted interventions, temporary coverage, and transitions back to assigned AMP Case Managers.
Build working relationships with resident leaders and relevant community organizations, and incorporate resident feedback into service planning and continuous improvement.
Monitor workload, scheduling, onsite coverage, staff availability, and cross-coverage needs; identify gaps and communicate staffing or service adjustments to the Director.
Review case management documentation and service data for accuracy, timeliness, and quality; provide staff feedback and corrective coaching when needed.
Monitor service outcomes, contract deliverables, and program reporting; help prepare timely and accurate information for leadership, MPHA, and funder reporting as assigned.
Support budget stewardship, staffing plans, and responsible use of program resources in coordination with the Director, Finance, and other agency partners.
Ensure assigned services follow applicable federal, state, local, agency, and MPHA contractual requirements and maintain appropriate confidentiality and professional boundaries.
Participate in program planning, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing refinement of the MPHA resident services model; identify opportunities to strengthen housing-focused, accessible services.
Represent Agate in MPHA operational meetings, resident service discussions, and community partnership meetings as assigned; elevate significant issues and decisions to the Director.
Travel to assigned MPHA properties and community service locations, including resident-facing visits when scheduled or appropriate.
Perform other related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Sociology, Public Administration, or a related field; or a minimum of three years of relevant professional experience in case management, housing stabilization, resident services, or related human services.
Minimum two years of experience managing human services or housing programs and supervising direct service staff.
Demonstrated ability to lead and support staff through clear expectations, respectful coaching, case consultation, accountability, and performance management.
Experience working with individuals and families facing housing instability or complex service needs, using trauma-informed, person-centered, and strengths-based approaches.
Ability to oversee multiple areas of program operations, including service quality, staff supervision, program evaluation, contract compliance, and resource oversight.
Strong relationship-building, communication, conflict-resolution, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with MPHA property management, residents, community partners, agency leadership, and interdisciplinary service teams.
Ability to review documentation and program data for completeness and quality, manage competing priorities, and use information to support service coordination and program oversight.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office products and ability to learn required case management and reporting systems.
Ability to accompany staff on home visits and provide direct resident support at assigned MPHA properties as needed.
Must possess a valid Minnesota driver's license, have access to a safe and reliable insured vehicle, and meet applicable driving.

Experience working in public housing, subsidized housing, supportive housing, or other community-based housing programs.

Experience implementing new programs, leading service transitions, or supporting organizational change.

At RELI Group, our work is grounded in purpose. jobs.description:
Description

ONSITE ONLY ***

Job Summary

Individuals within the Business Intelligence (BI) Analyst I role identify business intelligence, reporting, and data analysis needs. They work closely with clients and IT teams to turn data into critical information and knowledge that can be used to make sound business decisions. It is essential that BI Analysts build an understanding of the business at a level of detail that enables them to identify and address critical issues. They provide data that is accurate, congruent and reliable, and ensure the information is easily available to users for direct consumption or integration with other systems.

BI Analysts educate and train clients to use the data as an analytical tool, displaying the information in new forms and content for the purpose of analysis and option exploration.

BI Analysts work with clients to determine business requirements, priorities, define key performance indicators (KPI), and develop BI and data warehouse (DW) strategy. This includes working with business and development teams to design and document dashboards, alerts, and reports. This individual is accountable for providing leadership and independent initiatives in facilitating information gathering, structured documentation and presentation of findings to all levels of management. They conduct analyses of functional business processes and functional business requirements and participate in the development of business cases in the support of process changes and/or IT projects.

BI Analysts understand how data is turned into information and knowledge and how that knowledge supports and enables key business processes. They must have an in-depth understanding of the business environment and an interest in going beyond the obvious, delving into the source, the definition, philosophy, and foundational roots of a data element in order to create information. They must work well within a team environment.

Essential Duties

The duties listed below may not include all responsibilities that the person in this role may be asked to perform. Incumbent may be required to perform other related duties, as assigned, including cross training across other departments, as necessary.

Works on low to medium complexity tasks within one or more functional areas
Works on one or more tasks/projects as a team member and participates in or supports work-stream planning process
Works with internal and external customers and IT team members to gather and validate requirements
Develops and writes business requirements for the design of solutions
May determine and analyze commonly used queries and reports
Researches business problems and assists in the creation of models that help analyze these problems
Verifies the collected data is within required quality standards
May maintain the quality of metadata repository/data dictionary by adding, modifying and deleting data
Creates data quality tickets, as needed
Participates in job specific training and other various Bank training programs, as necessary
Maintains current knowledge of internal risk controls and loss prevention, including reporting of suspicious or unusual customer activity per Bank policy
Maintains current knowledge and complies with all federal and state laws and regulations and all established Bank policies and procedures, including internal audit controls related to department operations
Maintains current knowledge of all rules, regulations, and laws as they apply to BSA/OFAC/USA Patriot Act/CIP/AML

These specifications are general guidelines based on the minimum experience normally considered essential to the satisfactory performance of this position. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required to perform the position in a satisfactory manner. Individual abilities may result in some deviation from these guidelines.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Management or specialized training/certification, or equivalent work experience
Six (6) months to Two (2) years’ Business Analysis experience, or related education experience
Banking experience required
General Knowledge of business functional areas
Bilingual in English and Spanish is desired

This position reports to the Business Intelligence Team Lead
This position does not oversee other positions

jobs.description:
LEAD PEOPLE. DRIVE EXCELLENCE. MAKE AN IMPACT.

YMCA Y Scholars Program

Are you a leader who brings out the best in people, thrives on solving challenges, and knows how to turn a vision into results?

The YMCA of the East Bay is looking for a dynamic, driven, and people-centered Program Manager to lead our Y Scholars afterschool programs across multiple school communities.

We're looking for someone who doesn't just manage programs but builds strong teams, develops future leaders, takes ownership of challenges, and raises the standard of excellence.

In this role, you'll lead Site Coordinators, strengthen school partnerships, improve program operations, and help create exceptional learning experiences for hundreds of students.

You'll have the opportunity to make meaningful decisions, introduce new ideas, develop talented people, and shape the direction of our programs.

If you're ready to lead with purpose, take on meaningful challenges, and see the impact of your leadership every day, we want to meet you!

About the YMCA Y Scholars Program

We envision a world where every student discovers their purpose and achieves their full potential.
Each day, we elevate youth voice by offering enrichment opportunities that foster leadership, learning, and healthy habits.

Our Y Scholars Program serves elementary and middle school students through engaging afterschool experiences that promote academic achievement, physical activity, creative exploration, and social-emotional growth.

We believe that exceptional programs are built by exceptional teams. That's why we invest in developing our staff, fostering strong school partnerships, and creating a culture where people are empowered to grow, innovate, and succeed.

Does your mission align with ours?

Position Overview

Start Date:
Immediate
Compensation:
$74,000–$80,000 annually, depending on experience
Status:
Full-Time, Exempt
Typical Schedule:
Monday–Friday, 10:00 AM–6:30 PM
Locations:
Multiple elementary and middle school sites throughout West Contra Costa and Oakland
Map of Program Sites:
http://map.ymcayscholars.org

Position Benefits

Free YMCA gym membership
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Paid holidays and paid time off
YMCA retirement plan
Ongoing leadership development and professional training
Opportunities for career advancement within the YMCA

What You'll Do

As a Program Manager, you'll be responsible for the success of multiple school-based afterschool programs. You'll lead through your Site Coordinators, develop strong teams, and ensure our programs consistently deliver safe, engaging, and high-quality experiences for students.

This is a hands-on leadership role that combines people development, operational management, strategic problem-solving, and relationship building.

You'll spend your time coaching leaders, visiting program sites, strengthening systems, addressing challenges, and working with school and district partners to move our programs forward.
Most importantly, you'll help create a culture where team members feel supported, understand what's expected of them, take ownership of their work, and are motivated to deliver their best.

Your key responsibilities will include:

Lead and Develop Great Teams:
Supervise, mentor, and coach Site Coordinators and program staff. Build leadership capacity, strengthen performance, and create a culture of trust, accountability, and professional growth.
Champion Program Excellence:
Drive continuous improvement in program quality, student engagement, and learning experiences while ensuring alignment with YMCA standards and school district expectations.
Own Multi-Site Operations:
Oversee staffing, scheduling, program implementation, safety, and day-to-day operations across multiple school communities.
Set Expectations and Drive Accountability:
Establish clear performance standards, provide constructive feedback, address concerns promptly, and ensure teams follow through on commitments.
Build Strong School Partnerships:
Develop productive relationships with principals, district leaders, families, and community partners to strengthen collaboration and program success.
Manage Budgets and Resources:
Oversee program budgets, staffing allocations, purchasing, and resources to support efficient and financially responsible operations.
Turn Data Into Action:
Track enrollment, attendance, program performance, and compliance using Airtable, Google Workspace, and other systems. Identify trends and implement strategies to improve results.
Recruit and Grow Talent:
Lead hiring, onboarding, training, and staff development in partnership with YMCA Human Resources. Build a strong pipeline of future program leaders.
Strengthen Student and Family Experiences:
Support positive youth development, family engagement, effective behavior management, and responsive communication.
Solve Problems and Improve Systems:
Anticipate challenges, make informed decisions, implement practical solutions, and develop processes that help teams operate more effectively.
Advance the YMCA Mission:
Contribute to organizational initiatives, fundraising efforts, and opportunities to expand the impact of our programs.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a leader who knows that great management is about achieving results through people. You recognize opportunities, take initiative, and follow through.

You know how to encourage and support your team while also having the confidence to set boundaries, address performance concerns, and hold people accountable.

You can move comfortably between big-picture planning and the details of daily operations. When unexpected challenges arise, you stay focused, make thoughtful decisions, and help your team move forward.

Above all, you believe that developing people and delivering excellent programs go hand in hand.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in youth development, education, afterschool programs, expanded learning, or a related field
Minimum of 1 year of supervisory, management, or team leadership experience
Completion of at least 48 college units or a passing score on the California Instructional Aide Exam
Valid California driver's license and reliable transportation for regular travel between school sites
Ability to successfully complete DOJ/FBI background clearance
Ability to obtain CPR, First Aid, AED, and Child Abuse Prevention certifications within 30 days of hire (training provided)

You'll Thrive in This Role If You:

Bring Out the Best in People:
You enjoy coaching, mentoring, and helping others discover what they're capable of achieving.
Lead With Both Heart and Accountability:
You care about your team, communicate expectations clearly, and aren't afraid to have difficult conversations when needed.
Take Initiative and Ownership:
You see challenges as opportunities to act, rather than waiting for someone else to provide the solution.
Think Big and Execute Well:
You can translate ambitious goals into clear action plans, establish priorities, and deliver meaningful results.
Build Trust and Strong Relationships:
You connect authentically with people, navigate different perspectives, and collaborate effectively with staff, families, and school partners.
Make Decisions With Confidence:
You use sound judgment, seek relevant information, and take decisive action even when circumstances are changing.
Stay Organized and Adaptable:
You can manage multiple school sites, competing priorities, and unexpected situations without losing sight of what matters most.
Use Data to Get Better:
You pay attention to performance, ask thoughtful questions, and use information to improve programs and systems.
Communicate Clearly and Professionally:
You know how to provide feedback, resolve conflicts, and inspire others through effective communication.
Never Stop Growing:
You welcome feedback, reflect on your leadership, and continuously look for ways to improve yourself and your team.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described below are representative of those necessary to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

Sufficient strength, agility, and mobility to perform essential job duties and supervise program activities
Ability to occasionally lift up to 30 pounds
Frequent standing, walking, and bending throughout the workday
Ability to walk for extended periods and move between program spaces
Visual ability to effectively monitor activities in indoor and outdoor environments
Mobility to respond promptly to emergencies and other situations requiring immediate attention

Why Join Us?

At the YMCA, we believe that leadership is an opportunity to help others succeed while making a meaningful difference in our communities. As a Program Manager, you won't simply maintain existing programs. You'll have the opportunity to build something better, influence how our programs operate, and see the results of your leadership in the people and communities you serve.

Ready to Lead Something Meaningful?

Your leadership can inspire a team.
Your decisions can strengthen a program.
Your impact can change the experiences and opportunities of hundreds of students.

If you're ready for a leadership opportunity that challenges you to grow, empowers you to make decisions, and gives you the chance to create lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.

Job Profile Summary

Job Description

Salary Range:
$75,000 - $85,000 per year; DOE

About The University Innovation Alliance

The University Innovation Alliance is a national coalition of public research universities working together to improve student success and post graduate economic mobility, particularly for low-income students, first-generation college students, and students of color. UIA member institutions collaborate to design, test, refine, and scale practices that help more students persist, graduate, and successfully transition from college to careers. In 2025, the UIA aligned on expanded impact goals. One of the expanded goals is focused on improving value and mobility for students. The future ready graduates initiative is a direct result of the UIA now focusing on student success beyond degree completion. The UIA has secured 2 grant projects under this initiative and anticipates securing another 2 in the next year.

About Future Ready Graduates

Future Ready Graduates is UIA’s portfolio of work focused on helping member institutions expand and improve the number of work based learning experiences available to students to support their career preparation and employment outcomes. Current FRG projects are focused on work integrated learning redesign (focus on internships and project based learning) and student employment redesign leveraging a partnership with the Work + team at ASU. Through coordinated grant-funded initiatives, UIA supports campuses in redesigning student experiences, improving access to meaningful paid opportunities, strengthening employer partnerships, and connecting work-based learning more directly to persistence, completion, and career outcomes.

Position Summary

The Grant Program Manager, Future Ready Graduates is responsible for the day-to-day delivery, implementation, coordination, and program management of UIA’s Future Ready Graduates grant portfolio. The position will initially manage delivery of two active awards and may assume responsibility for up to two additional awards.

The Program Manager will coordinate participating campuses, partners, consultants, employers, and internal UIA contributors to ensure that project activities are completed on time, meet funder commitments, and achieve the expected level of quality. This role will maintain project plans, monitor campus progress, facilitate meetings and events, organize employer feedback processes, maintain accurate records in Salesforce and Google Drive, and represent program implementation during funder meetings and written updates.

The ideal candidate is a highly organized and collaborative program manager who can manage multiple grants and campus workstreams simultaneously. This person will be skilled at setting clear expectations, holding partners accountable, identifying risks early, and helping campus teams translate project requirements into practical implementation.

Key Responsibilities

Grant Portfolio Management

Manage the implementation and operations of two active Future Ready Graduates awards, with the potential to manage up to two additional related awards.
Translate grant agreements, workplans, budgets, milestones, and funder commitments into coordinated implementation plans.
Develop and maintain project plans that identify activities, owners, deadlines, dependencies, decision points, and required deliverables.
Monitor implementation across all assigned awards and provide regular updates on progress, risks, delays, and resource needs.
Ensure work is delivered on time, within the approved scope, and at the level of quality expected by UIA and its funding partners.
Coordinate overlapping activities and shared deliverables across awards so that the Future Ready Graduates portfolio operates as a cohesive body of work.
Support grant launch, implementation, reporting, evaluation, dissemination, and closeout activities.

Campus Implementation and Accountability

Serve as a primary point of contact for campus teams participating in assigned Future Ready Graduates projects.
Lead campus onboarding and establish clear expectations for participation, implementation, reporting, and deliverable quality.
Help campuses translate grant requirements into campus-specific implementation plans, milestones, and workstreams.
Monitor progress toward campus deliverables and follow up regularly to address missed deadlines, incomplete work, or implementation barriers.
Review campus submissions and project materials for completeness, alignment, and quality.
Coordinate coaching, technical assistance, and problem-solving support with ASU Work+, consultants, evaluators, and other subject-matter experts.
Maintain regular communication with campus leads and ensure institutional teams remain engaged throughout the project period.

Employer Engagement and Feedback Loops

Work with UIA colleagues and campus teams to recruit and engage employers as project advisors, co-design partners, and sources of ongoing feedback.
Establish and maintain structured employer feedback loops across the Future Ready Graduates portfolio.
Plan employer listening sessions, validation meetings, feedback activities, and other engagement opportunities.
Ensure employer perspectives inform program design, student journey redesign, implementation testing, and refinement.
Document employer feedback and help campus teams translate it into actionable program or system improvements.
Track how employer input influences campus decisions and project outcomes. Employer feedback is intended to be embedded throughout the redesign cycle, including discovery, prototype validation, implementation, and planning for scale.

Meetings, Convenings, and Project Events

Plan and coordinate project-based meetings, campus working sessions, communities of practice, workshops, employer sessions, and in-person convenings.
Develop agendas, participant materials, timelines, run-of-show documents, and follow-up communications.
Facilitate selected meetings and working sessions and coordinate facilitation by ASU Work+, consultants, or other partners.
Organize cross-campus learning opportunities that allow institutions to compare progress, troubleshoot barriers, and refine their approaches.
Coordinate event logistics in partnership with UIA’s Campus Engagement & Events Manager and operations staff.
Capture decisions, action items, and follow-up responsibilities after project meetings.

Funder Engagement and Reporting

Prepare updates, project summaries, briefing materials, and talking points for funder meetings.
Maintain documentation needed to demonstrate progress against funder commitments.
Identify risks or changes that may require early communication, funder guidance, or formal approval.
Support preparation of continuation requests, change requests, final reports, and grant-closeout materials.

Project Records and Knowledge Management

Maintain complete, accurate, and current project records in Salesforce and Google Drive.
Establish and maintain a clear folder structure, naming conventions, version-control practices, and documentation standards.
Record campus participation, meetings, milestones, deliverables, decisions, risks, employer engagement, and follow-up activities in Salesforce.
Ensure key documents, reports, workplans, participant materials, and final deliverables are stored consistently and accessible to the appropriate team members.
Maintain project calendars, trackers, contact lists, reporting schedules, and shared implementation tools.
Support development of standard templates and processes that can be used across the Future Ready Graduates portfolio.

Progress Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Capture

Track progress toward grant milestones, deliverables, campus participation targets, and intended outcomes.
Coordinate collection of implementation updates, participation data, feedback, and supporting documentation from campuses and partners.
Work with evaluators and internal partners to ensure campuses understand data requirements and submit information on schedule.
Identify common implementation barriers, promising practices, and conditions that influence success across participating institutions.
Help translate project learning into case studies, playbooks, implementation guides, employer-feedback resources, and other materials for broader diffusion.
Support final evaluation, synthesis, dissemination, and planning for scale.
Design and develop evaluation frameworks, data collection instruments, templates, surveys, interview protocols, rubrics, dashboards, and reporting processes that enable campuses to consistently collect, analyze, and use implementation and outcome data.
Design AI-enabled workflows that transform complex institutional data into actionable insights, scalable evaluation processes, and decision-making resources.

The Future Ready Graduates work plan calls for shared resources such as campus case studies, dashboard guidance, employer feedback-loop templates, implementation guidance, and a strategy for broader diffusion.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Establish clear ownership, review processes, and deadlines for work requiring contributions from multiple teams.
Coordinate with the Business Operations & Finance Manager on budgets, campus stipends, contracts, and grant-related financial processes.
