Job Description & Summary

At PwC, our people in project portfolio management focus on optimising project portfolios to drive strategic business outcomes. These individuals oversee project selection, prioritisation, and resource allocation to facilitate successful project delivery.

In project management at PwC, you will oversee and coordinate various projects to facilitate successful delivery within budget and timeline. You will leverage strong organisational and communication skills to effectively manage teams and stakeholders.

About the Team

The Capital Project Services (CPS) team is made up of skilled professionals with expertise in delivering capital projects across a variety of sectors, including Energy, Utilities, and Resource, Transport, Oil & Gas and Government & Healthcare. We help clients maximise the value of their projects and businesses by providing the knowledge and support needed to navigate complex and challenging situations.

Role Overview

As a CPS Manager, you will design and implement effective project and programme management strategies for clients across multiple industries. You will work closely with senior leaders of major global organisations to improve the efficiency of their capital programmes, support the achievement of project objectives, and provide guidance to clients managing projects within tight budget constraints. You will also assist clients in overcoming project delivery challenges. The role will be predominately focussed on the UK market, which you will typically support remotely from the ETIC. Candidates should be available to travel regionally and to the UK, although this will not be required regularly. 

Key Responsibilities

• Manage multiple client engagements simultaneously, reporting to senior members of staff, both in ETIC and the UK. 

• Lead, mentor, and develop junior team members, providing training and guidance as required.

• Build and maintain strong working relationships with clients, acting as a key point of contact.

• Contribute to the technical development of both yourself and the wider team, ensuring up-to-date knowledge of industry best practices.

• Stay informed about local and national business and economic trends relevant to capital projects.

• Participate in business development activities, including identifying and researching new opportunities with existing and prospective clients.

• Foster strong internal relationships and actively promote the CPS team’s capabilities within the firm.

Types of Engagements you will work on:

CPS assists clients with a broad range of challenges relating to their capital programmes. We are constantly adapting our approach to meet our clients needs and challenges. Some typical engagements are as follows:

• Programme Recovery and Turnaround : Supporting a public sector client whose major infrastructure programme was facing significant delays and cost overruns. Conduct a comprehensive review, identify root causes, and implement a recovery plan to bring the programme back on track.

• Capital Programme Optimisation : Work with a utility company to review and optimise their capital investment portfolio. This includes prioritising projects, streamlining governance processes, and introducing new performance management tools to maximise return on investment.

• Digital Transformation of Project Controls : Assist a infrastructure asset owner in implementing digital project controls across their capital projects portfolio. Selecting and deploying new project management software, training staff, and embedding new ways of working to improve transparency and reporting.

• Procurement and Supply Chain Strategy : Advising a utilities company on the development and execution of a new procurement and supply chain strategy for a multi-billion-pound capital programme. Support supplier selection, contract negotiations, and the establishment of robust commercial management processes.

• Independent Project Assurance:  Providing independent assurance to a client on the delivery of a major capital project. Including regular health checks, risk assessments, and recommendations to improve project governance and delivery confidence.

Candidate Profile We are seeking a candidate who:

• Communicates confidently and delivers clear, impactful messages to a range of audiences to influence outcomes.

• Demonstrates leadership skills and a strong commitment to coaching and developing others.

• Possesses strong technical and analytical abilities, with the capacity to simplify complex issues and deliver practical client solutions.

• Is passionate about capital project delivery and motivated to learn from colleagues and build collaborative relationships at all levels.

• Has a solid academic background and relevant industry experience, with a commitment to ongoing professional development.

• Is willing to travel nationally and internationally as required.

• Proven ability to lead, manage, or work effectively within teams to deliver projects and solutions.

• Experience managing contracts, suppliers, or projects, with a thorough understanding of the core principles underpinning successful project delivery.

• A commitment to continuous personal and team development.

• Management consulting experience, including the design and implementation of operating and delivery models.

• Experience in digital transformation or technology consulting.

new_jobs.title: Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Description – Business Analyst

Role overview

We are hiring a Business Analyst to own how our systems, data and processes work together — from gathering requirements to building, automating, reporting and training, with AI used as a core part of how the work gets done.

On any given day you may map a process, write a spec, build an automation, fix a CRM layout, produce a dashboard, run a project stand-up or train a team. You will act as the bridge between the business and the tech stack, and turn messy problems into clear, working solutions.

Key responsibilities

AI-led delivery (day to day)

Use AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Zia) daily to speed up requirements, documentation, analysis, testing and build work.

Design and deploy AI-powered workflows: agents, assistants, classification, summarisation, data enrichment and AI-generated content inside business systems.

Write, test and maintain prompts and prompt templates; evaluate AI output for accuracy, tone and risk before it reaches staff or customers.

Connect AI models to business systems through APIs, MCP servers and automation platforms.

Proactively identify where AI can replace manual tasks, and measure time saved.

Keep up with new AI tools and features, run quick pilots and recommend what to adopt.

Apply responsible AI practice: data privacy, access control, human review and clear usage guidelines.

Business analysis (functional and technical)

Run stakeholder workshops and interviews to capture requirements, pain points and success criteria.

Map current-state and future-state processes; identify gaps, waste, automation and AI opportunities.

Write clear BRDs, functional specs, user stories, acceptance criteria and technical specs (data models, field mappings, API and integration logic).

Translate business needs into system configuration and build‑ready designs, and validate delivered work against requirements.

Data analysis and business intelligence

Clean, audit and maintain data quality across CRM and operational systems (duplicates, picklists, field hygiene, ownership).

Build and maintain dashboards, KPIs and recurring reports for leadership and operational teams.

Use AI-assisted analysis to surface trends, insights and recommended actions.

Write queries and data transformations to support reporting and decision-making.

Project management

Plan and deliver system and process projects end to end: scope, timeline, risks, dependencies and sign-off.

Run sprints, stand-ups and status updates; keep tasks, priorities and blockers visible.

Manage multiple concurrent workstreams and re-prioritise quickly as business needs change.

Automation and integration

Design and build workflow automations, blueprints and custom functions (e.g. Zoho Deluge, Make.com scenarios, GoHighLevel workflows).

Build and maintain integrations between platforms using APIs, webhooks and connectors.

Identify and implement AI and automation opportunities that remove manual work.

Monitor automations for failures and fix them quickly.

Tech stack management and system administration

Administer core platforms: users, roles, profiles, permissions, modules, layouts, fields and templates.

Maintain the tech stack inventory, licences, access and vendor relationships; recommend tools to add, consolidate or retire.

Own change management: test in sandbox, document changes and release safely.

Handle tier‑2 system support and troubleshooting for internal users.

Training, documentation and best practice

Create SOPs, user guides, process maps and training materials for every system or process change, using AI to produce and maintain them faster.

Deliver onboarding and refresher training to staff, live and recorded.

Define and enforce system, data and AI standards, naming conventions and governance; train staff to use AI tools effectively and safely.

Team management

Lead, guide and review the work of junior analysts, admins or offshore support staff.

Allocate tasks, set priorities and quality‑check output.

Coach team members and contribute to hiring and onboarding new team members.

Requirements

Must have

3–5 years in a business analyst, systems analyst or business systems role, covering both functional and technical BA work.

Demonstrated daily use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or similar) to accelerate analysis, documentation and build work, with examples to show.

Hands‑on experience building AI-powered automations: calling LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and embedding AI steps into workflows (e.g. via Make.com, Zoho Flow or n8n).

Sound judgement on AI output quality, data privacy and when human review is needed.

Hands‑on administration of at least one major CRM (Zoho CRM strongly preferred; Salesforce or HubSpot considered).

Proven experience building workflow automations and integrations (APIs, webhooks, JSON, low-code tools such as Make.com, Zapier or Zoho Flow).

Strong data skills: Excel / Google Sheets (advanced), SQL or similar query language, and a BI tool (Zoho Analytics, Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau).

Experience managing projects with defined scope, timelines and stakeholders, using tools such as Zoho Projects, Jira or Asana.

Experience writing requirements, user stories, process maps (BPMN or swimlane) and SOPs.

Experience delivering user training and supporting adoption of new systems.

Excellent written and spoken English.

Nice to have

Scripting experience (Zoho Deluge, JavaScript or Python).

Advanced AI experience: building AI agents, MCP servers, RAG / knowledge-base assistants or multi-step AI workflows.

Experience across the wider Zoho One suite (Desk, Recruit, Creator, Sprints, Learn, Cliq).

Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 administration.

Prior experience leading or mentoring a small team.

Experience supporting Australian businesses or working with remote teams across time zones.

Relevant certification (e.g. Zoho CRM Certified Administrator, IIBA ECBA/CCBA, PMP/CAPM, Agile/Scrum, or an AI/LLM course).

What we’re looking for

AI-first mindset.

Your default question is "how can AI make this faster or better?", and you back it with working solutions.

Strong communicator.

You explain technical ideas in plain language, write clearly, ask the right questions and keep stakeholders informed without being chased.

Highly organised.

You juggle many requests, prioritise by impact and urgency, and keep your work documented and traceable.

Fast turnaround.

You move quickly, deliver in iterations and don't let small tasks sit.

Multi-dimensional problem solver.

You consider the process, the people, the data and the system together, not just the immediate symptom.

Solution- and process-driven.

You bring a recommended fix, not just a problem, and you design repeatable processes rather than one‑off workarounds.

Ownership mindset.

You take responsibility end to end, from requirement to adoption, and work well with limited supervision.

new_jobs.title: Protective Intelligence Analyst- OSINT Monitoring and Triage
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly capable Protective Intelligence Analyst to support the protection of senior Vanguard executives globally. This role requires an experienced OSINT practitioner who can independently manage threat identification and triage, prioritize competing executive protection needs, and produce decision-ready intelligence products under time pressure. The position owns the threat identification and initial assessment function for Vanguard’s protective intelligence program, including the daily monitoring and alert queue through which every inbound threat communication, platform alert, and referral receives its initial assessment. The Protective Intelligence Analyst will distinguish credible concerns from noise, open cases for identified security concerns, and manage case tracking and related metrics for the program. The role offers broad exposure across the protective intelligence lifecycle and meaningful ownership of threat intake, applying structured analytic judgment to determine which matters warrant escalation or further investigation.

Monitoring & Triage

Manage daily alert and intake queues: vendor alerting feeds, the program’s intake channels, executive-assistant and partner referrals, and regional intelligence routing.
Triage inbound items against the program’s established threat screening criteria; disposition items as unfounded with documented rationale or open cases for investigation.
Provide dedicated monitoring coverage during executive travel and event windows, assessing emerging developments in real time and escalating per defined criteria.
Maintain watchlist hygiene and help fine tune OSINT feeds to ensure reliable threat identification.

Case Management & Intelligence Production

Maintain key protective intelligence trackers/metrics: request log, alert log, case entries, product IDs, and dashboard integrity.
Conduct OSINT collection and analysis for protective intelligence assessments, documenting sources and findings and contributing analytic judgments to final products.
Draft the program’s weekly intelligence summary, synthesizing alert activity, case developments, and emerging threat trends into concise, decision-ready reporting.
Process intake acknowledgements and maintain records-handling standards for intake channels.

Team Model – Primary Focus, Universal Capability

Triage and monitoring is the primary focus of this role, not an exclusive lane. Every Protective Intelligence Analyst trains to produce the program’s core assessment products to standard, rotates through triage and monitoring coverage, and serves as designated backup for at least one other product line, so the team carries no single points of failure.
Cross-train teammates in triage and monitoring, maintain current proficiency in teammates’ specialties, and participate in the program’s dual-review and after-action practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security studies, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Minimum of three years of related experience in a field such as intelligence analysis, GSOC/watch operations, journalism/research, or military/law-enforcement analysis.
Demonstrated ability to work a high-volume queue with consistency, accuracy, and documented decisions.
Strong OSINT skills, including the ability to locate, verify, and assess the credibility of information across open sources.
Comfort with reading concerning or threatening content professionally and escalating appropriately.
High ethical standards and discretion when handling sensitive executive and corporate information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders clearly and calmly under time pressure.
Proven ability to think critically and assess incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with threat intelligence, alerting, or case management platforms.
Formal training or applied experience in threat assessment, targeted violence prevention, or intelligence analysis.
ATAP membership, with active interest or progress toward obtaining the Certified Threat Manager (CTM) designation.

Special Factors

Participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours escalation support as the program matures.
Early-morning queue coverage; occasional evening and weekend surge coverage during executive travel windows.
Occasional domestic travel (

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

Collect and manage information from diverse sources such as social media platforms, messaging apps, forums, the dark web, news feeds, and other open and covert channels.

3+ years of experience in intelligence analysis, with a focus on WEBINT / OSINT.

Strong understanding of Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI), the cybercrime ecosystem, and underground information sources.

Excellent analytical thinking and report-writing skills

We are seeking a highly capable Protective Intelligence Analyst to support the protection of senior Vanguard executives globally. This role requires an experienced OSINT practitioner who can independently manage threat identification and triage, prioritize competing executive protection needs, and produce decision-ready intelligence products under time pressure. The position owns the threat identification and initial assessment function for Vanguard’s protective intelligence program, including the daily monitoring and alert queue through which every inbound threat communication, platform alert, and referral receives its initial assessment. The Protective Intelligence Analyst will distinguish credible concerns from noise, open cases for identified security concerns, and manage case tracking and related metrics for the program. The role offers broad exposure across the protective intelligence lifecycle and meaningful ownership of threat intake, applying structured analytic judgment to determine which matters warrant escalation or further investigation.

Monitoring & Triage

Manage daily alert and intake queues: vendor alerting feeds, the program’s intake channels, executive-assistant and partner referrals, and regional intelligence routing.
Triage inbound items against the program’s established threat screening criteria; disposition items as unfounded with documented rationale or open cases for investigation.
Provide dedicated monitoring coverage during executive travel and event windows, assessing emerging developments in real time and escalating per defined criteria.
Maintain watchlist hygiene and help fine tune OSINT feeds to ensure reliable threat identification.

Case Management & Intelligence Production

Maintain key protective intelligence trackers/metrics: request log, alert log, case entries, product IDs, and dashboard integrity.
Conduct OSINT collection and analysis for protective intelligence assessments, documenting sources and findings and contributing analytic judgments to final products.
Draft the program’s weekly intelligence summary, synthesizing alert activity, case developments, and emerging threat trends into concise, decision-ready reporting.
Process intake acknowledgements and maintain records-handling standards for intake channels.

Team Model – Primary Focus, Universal Capability

Triage and monitoring is the primary focus of this role, not an exclusive lane. Every Protective Intelligence Analyst trains to produce the program’s core assessment products to standard, rotates through triage and monitoring coverage, and serves as designated backup for at least one other product line, so the team carries no single points of failure.
Cross-train teammates in triage and monitoring, maintain current proficiency in teammates’ specialties, and participate in the program’s dual-review and after-action practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security studies, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience).

Demonstrated ability to work a high-volume queue with consistency, accuracy, and documented decisions.
Strong OSINT skills, including the ability to locate, verify, and assess the credibility of information across open sources.
Comfort with reading concerning or threatening content professionally and escalating appropriately.
High ethical standards and discretion when handling sensitive executive and corporate information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders clearly and calmly under time pressure.
Proven ability to think critically and assess incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with threat intelligence, alerting, or case management platforms.
Formal training or applied experience in threat assessment, targeted violence prevention, or intelligence analysis.
ATAP membership, with active interest or progress toward obtaining the Certified Threat Manager (CTM) designation.

Individuals within the Business Intelligence (BI) Analyst I role identify business intelligence, reporting, and data analysis needs. Each day, we elevate youth voice by offering enrichment opportunities that foster leadership, learning, and healthy habits.

Our Y Scholars Program serves elementary and middle school students through engaging afterschool experiences that promote academic achievement, physical activity, creative exploration, and social-emotional growth.

Above all, you believe that developing people and delivering excellent programs go hand in hand.

Required Qualifications

Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in youth development, education, afterschool programs, expanded learning, or a related field
Minimum of 1 year of supervisory, management, or team leadership experience
Completion of at least 48 college units or a passing score on the California Instructional Aide Exam
Valid California driver's license and reliable transportation for regular travel between school sites
Ability to successfully complete DOJ/FBI background clearance
Ability to obtain CPR, First Aid, AED, and Child Abuse Prevention certifications within 30 days of hire (training provided)

You'll Thrive in This Role If You:

Bring Out the Best in People:
You enjoy coaching, mentoring, and helping others discover what they're capable of achieving.
Lead With Both Heart and Accountability:
You care about your team, communicate expectations clearly, and aren't afraid to have difficult conversations when needed.
Take Initiative and Ownership:
You see challenges as opportunities to act, rather than waiting for someone else to provide the solution.
Think Big and Execute Well:
You can translate ambitious goals into clear action plans, establish priorities, and deliver meaningful results.
Build Trust and Strong Relationships:
You connect authentically with people, navigate different perspectives, and collaborate effectively with staff, families, and school partners.
Make Decisions With Confidence:
You use sound judgment, seek relevant information, and take decisive action even when circumstances are changing.
Stay Organized and Adaptable:
You can manage multiple school sites, competing priorities, and unexpected situations without losing sight of what matters most.
Use Data to Get Better:
You pay attention to performance, ask thoughtful questions, and use information to improve programs and systems.
Communicate Clearly and Professionally:
You know how to provide feedback, resolve conflicts, and inspire others through effective communication.
Never Stop Growing:
You welcome feedback, reflect on your leadership, and continuously look for ways to improve yourself and your team.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described below are representative of those necessary to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

Sufficient strength, agility, and mobility to perform essential job duties and supervise program activities
Ability to occasionally lift up to 30 pounds
Frequent standing, walking, and bending throughout the workday
Ability to walk for extended periods and move between program spaces
Visual ability to effectively monitor activities in indoor and outdoor environments
Mobility to respond promptly to emergencies and other situations requiring immediate attention

Why Join Us?

At the YMCA, we believe that leadership is an opportunity to help others succeed while making a meaningful difference in our communities. As a Program Manager, you won't simply maintain existing programs. You'll have the opportunity to build something better, influence how our programs operate, and see the results of your leadership in the people and communities you serve.

Ready to Lead Something Meaningful?

Your leadership can inspire a team.
Your decisions can strengthen a program.
Your impact can change the experiences and opportunities of hundreds of students.

If you're ready for a leadership opportunity that challenges you to grow, empowers you to make decisions, and gives you the chance to create lasting impact, we encourage you to apply.
